$comment: Every Tauri command this application registers, and who consumes it.
Checked by scripts/check-ipc.mjs, which fails when a command is registered
without an entry here, when an entry names a command that is no longer
registered, or when the frontend invokes a handler that does not exist.
frontend         - called from src/. The checker verifies this.
admin            - operator- or support-invoked, deliberately not on a page.
external         - for an embedding host, not for this application's UI.
frontend-pending - the backend half exists and no surface calls it yet.
A command with no consumer at all is not a state this file can express.
That is the point: adding one means choosing which of the four it is and
writing down why, in front of whoever reviews the change.

agent_export_artifact.note: Called from src/. Copies a produced file to a destination the person chose in the OS save dialog.

agent_resume_run.note: Continues an interrupted run under its own run id, so the resumption's events, checkpoint and effect ledger extend the original history rather than starting a second one. Checks resumability first and refuses on any disagreement between the checkpoint and the world now. Drives the same execution path as agent_start_run via the shared internal driver. The Tasks screen's recovery flow that would call it is still to be built.

agent_run_resumability.note: Reports whether a run can be resumed. Same flow as agent_resume_run.

agent_telemetry_health.note: Proves the telemetry chain without writing to it. Replaces the synthetic <startup> model call; a diagnostic, deliberately not on a page.

artifact_bytes.note: Called from src/. Returns a produced file's bytes as base64 so the chat can render a PDF in place.

detect_system_models.note: Called from src/. The Storage screen's scan for weight files already on the machine; it registers what the manifest does not list, adding only and never editing an entry an administrator wrote by hand. Gated on ImportModel because it writes the manifest.

get_all_package_certifications.note: Every certification on this machine. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_compatible_packages.note: Packages that will run, certified or not. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_default_config.note: Returns the shipped defaults so a support engineer can diff a broken config against them.

get_experimental_packages.note: Packages known not to be certified. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_model_recommendations.note: Ranks models against a fresh hardware scan. Its only caller was recommendation.service.ts, which no component imported; the Models screen does its own sizing. Kept because the ranking is real and the screen should use it. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_package_certification.note: Certification for one model package. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_recommended_packages.note: Certified packages this hardware can run. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

get_runtime_profile.note: The runtime profile a package declares. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

list_library_models.note: Called from src/. Distinct from list_registered_models, which returns the registry as loaded at startup: this one re-reads the manifest from disk, so a model detect_system_models registered moments ago shows up on the Storage screen without a restart.

log_activity.note: Lets an embedding host write an attributed line into the audit chain.

notebook_add_documents.note: Called from src/. Reads files through the same attachment pipeline a chat turn uses and puts them in a notebook.

notebook_assertions.note: Called from src/. The directed relationship claims over a notebook, with their provenance, review status, direction certainty and evidence.

notebook_bind_conversation.note: Called from src/. Records that a conversation belongs to a notebook, so reopening the notebook restores its own thread rather than whatever the general chat was last on.

notebook_build_graph.note: Called from src/. Runs the statistical extraction pass over a notebook's documents; resumable, skips documents already built at this extractor version.

notebook_clear_conversation_scope.note: Called from src/. Takes the notebook off a conversation and leaves its evidence alone. Deliberately not notebook_unbind, which also deletes every research manifest in the thread and would stop the citations in answers already given from resolving.

notebook_conversation_scope.note: Called from src/. The notebook and selection a conversation was left on, for restoring the chip above the composer.

notebook_correct_assertion.note: Called from src/. Corrects a relationship's wording or which way round it runs; the result is the person's own accepted claim.

notebook_create_assertion.note: Called from src/. Records a relationship a person asserts themselves. It has no passage behind it and every surface that uses it says so.

notebook_create_note.note: Called from src/. Creates a note a person writes themselves, which carries no evidence and is never reported as source-verified.

notebook_delete.note: Called from src/. Deletes a notebook and the graph built over it; the documents are untouched.

notebook_delete_assertion.note: Called from src/. Deletes a relationship a person added by hand. Model proposals are rejected rather than deleted.

notebook_delete_note.note: Called from src/. Deletes one of a notebook's notes.

notebook_extract_relations.note: Called from src/. Names a notebook's edges with Babelscape/rebel-large in a CPU sidecar. It may only name an edge the statistical pass already found, never add one, and a relation outside a curated Wikidata subset is dropped and counted.

notebook_graph.note: Called from src/. Returns a local or global view of a notebook's graph, with the notebook's files as nodes joined to the terms found in them unless withDocuments is false.

notebook_node_evidence.note: Called from src/. The passages behind one node, so the interface can answer 'why do you think that?'.

notebook_notes.note: Called from src/. The notes and generated reports a notebook holds.

notebook_open_citation.note: Called from src/. Resolves one [En] marker against the turn's stored manifest and returns the passage as used plus the page as it reads now, reporting removed, changed and unreadable sources as distinct states.

notebook_remove_document.note: Called from src/. Takes one document out of a notebook, with the graph evidence that came from it.

notebook_rename.note: Called from src/. Renames a notebook the signed-in person owns.

notebook_render_subgraph.note: Renders a chosen subgraph as Markdown. No longer used by the Notebooks screen: 'Ask about selection' now sends the graph node ids as a research scope and the backend retrieves the original passages, so the answer cites documents rather than a summary of a graph. Kept registered for export, and unreferenced from src/ until an export surface exists.

notebook_repair_source.note: Called from src/. Records the notebook access a membership row was written without, so a source whose text is already on disk becomes readable. Re-reads nothing and runs no model; refuses anything that is not repairable this way.

notebook_review_assertion.note: Called from src/. Accepts or rejects one extracted relationship. A rejection keeps the row, so a later extraction pass cannot re-propose the same claim with nothing to say it was refused.

notebook_save_answer.note: Called from src/. Saves an assistant answer into the notebook with the evidence it used. The body is read from the conversation store, never from the caller, so nothing else can be saved as a cited answer.

notebook_scope_preview.note: Called from src/. What the next question would read — how many sources, which are unreadable, what the graph selection narrows it to, and how passages will be found — so the scope is visible before the question is asked rather than after it is answered.

notebook_set_conversation_scope.note: Called from src/. Remembers which notebook a chat is asking and which of its sources, so reopening the conversation restores the chip. The preference only -- each turn freezes its own scope onto its evidence manifest.

notebook_source_page.note: Called from src/. One page of a notebook source's extracted text, for the reader. Scoped to the notebook as well as the owner, so a document held in another notebook is not readable through this one.

notebook_source_status.note: Called from src/. Whether each source in a notebook can actually be read, with the reason and the repair when it cannot. Distinct from notebook_documents, which answers membership and says nothing about whether any of it has readable text.

notebook_threads.note: Called from src/. The conversations started from one notebook, skipping bindings whose conversation has since been deleted.

notebook_turn_evidence.note: Called from src/. The evidence manifest one answer was built on: which chunk, which document, which page, at which extraction revision. Returns null for a turn that was not notebook-scoped.

notebook_type_graph.note: Called from src/. Asks an already-loaded local model to type a notebook's terms and name relations; every claim must cite a passage and quote it, and anything unverified is dropped and counted.

notebook_update_note.note: Called from src/. Edits a note. The saved-body hash is not refreshed, so an edited answer starts reporting that it has been edited rather than keeping the standing it earned before the edit.

reload_certification_packs.note: Re-reads the certification packs after an operator installs one. No surface calls it yet; the service wrapper that did was dead code and was removed.

run_benchmark.note: Refuses: the measured path is not wired. It previously timed nothing and recorded the caller's own arguments as a measurement, so it now returns an error rather than a plausible row. Operator-invoked; never on a page, because a benchmark started by a render is a benchmark of the render.

sign_provenance.note: Signs an evidence package. Part of the export flow, driven by an operator.

skill_reload.note: Re-reads the skills directory after an operator installs or edits one.

skill_search.note: Lists installed skills as cards. The model reaches skills through capability.search; this is the operator's view.

subagent_profiles.note: Lists the loaded subagent profiles, so an operator can see which are available.

verify_provenance.note: Verifies a signed evidence package received from elsewhere.

voice_speak.note: Voice output. The sidecar and command exist; no surface calls them yet.

widget_prepare.note: Called from src/components/chat/WidgetFrame.tsx. Holds one widget document in memory and returns the id the widget:// handler serves it under.

zero_trust_check_tool_call.note: Asks the zero-trust gate about a call on behalf of an embedding host.

zero_trust_confirm_approval.note: Confirms an approval decision through the zero-trust gate.
